newsitem.title: USA: China's BBB rating not affected by Deng death -S&P.
newsitem.headline: China's BBB rating not affected by Deng death -S&P.

text.p: The death of China's senior leader Deng Xiaoping will not adversely impact its BBB foreign currency credit rating, Standard & Poor's said on Thursday.
In fact, S&P said its outlook on China remains positive.

S&P noted Deng's participation in decision-making process had been steadily declining and the transition in China's leadership has been underway for years. The final stage of transfer of power should not lead to a major disruption in Chinese politics or a disruption in the continued development of the Chinese economy, the agency said.

"The death of Deng will complete the de facto transfer of power to Communist Party leader Jiang Zemin," said S&P China analyst Guido Cipriani. "While Jiang does not have the standing of revolutionary leaders such as Deng and Mao, Jiang and the core leadership group have entrenched themselves over recent years."
The entrenchment should ensure overall policy stability during the transition, Cipriani said.
Paul Coughlin, managing director at S&P, said Jiang's primacy may be vulnerable over the medium term, but that the group's commitment to stability should not be underestimated.

"While there may be tensions within the Party leadership relating to personalities and policies, policy disputes generally relate to the pace of change and generally do not reflect a desire to abandon or roll back reform," he said.
